title: Ikasha, She Who Sleeps
subtitle: The Hush Before the Choice

lore.description:
Ikasha is the hush between footfalls, the patience of dark water, the black-feathered watcher at every threshold. In stillness she gathers what might be, at crossroads she whispers of what may yet come. Ravens circle her, bearing secrets between worlds. Her followers learn to move unseen and speak unremembered, becoming shadows that slip between what is and what could be.

**The name left unspoken in company.**

Some Tulkani households speak of Ikasha as an aunt who must not be woken, though the relationship belongs to their telling and does not supply a universal divine family tree. A child learns to lower their voice beside a sleeping traveler before learning any prayer. The space given to someone who cannot yet speak becomes a way to approach She Who Sleeps.

These household observances traveled with people taking shelter beyond their own circles. A host who leaves a guest unquestioned may be honoring Ikasha or simply observing courtesy. The distinction often matters less to the guest than it does to an official seeking a testimony. Nobody acquires the right to someone's hidden history by offering a bed.

**The Bell-Shrouded and the Deep Listener.**

Mistlands keepers know the Bell-Shrouded at the pause in work when a sound should have reached the next station and has not. They check the rope, ask who last heard the bell, and lower their voices. The unknotted rope carries its established meaning without requiring a theory of the fog. An outsider who names every silence an omen is less useful than a neighbor who notices which silence is new.

Aeler Deep Listener observances developed around descents into unfamiliar workings. One person remains above long enough to hear the first report. The role is inherited differently across ranges: a severe high hold may insist on a keeper's silence, while a foothill crew talks until the signal arrives. Both make space for information that has not yet returned. Forgotten undervaults give the practice local histories; they are not all chambers in one known design.

**The Tide Watcher in Zakov.**

Zakov's smugglers carried the Unlit Candle into rooms where a stranger could wait for a boat without being visible from the quay. Older attendants remember the practice as shelter for people escaping searches. Later patrons have used the same rooms to store illicit cargo and call that continuity. The keepers disagree over whether they are preserving a refuge or renting its reputation.

A successful Tide Watcher may know exactly which official searches a door and still refuse a client's request to have that official killed. The practice preserves an opening. It does not require eliminating everyone who might close it. Another keeper may regard that distinction as a luxury bought with somebody else's danger.

**A silence with an ending.**

On Sihai's caravan approaches, Ikasha's quiet rooms shelter people whose documents cannot yet establish where they belong. Some attendants work discreetly with clerks to recover a record; others believe any returned record will restore the danger. The person waiting may want recognition more than either helper expects.

Aveh can offer departure from a former identity; Ikasha's followers can keep a possibility open until a person chooses. Neither course is harmless by definition. Begin with a witness hiding under a borrowed name who now wants to speak for a condemned relative. Their host knows what the disclosure could destroy. Ikasha does not issue an order deciding which silence should end, and the host's fear must not become proof that the witness has no choice.
lore.followers: Ikasha does not act; she waits. She does not command; she suggests. Her power is not in force but in possibility – the hidden door, the forgotten name, the secret that, if spoken, would change everything. Those who serve her become keepers of thresholds, listeners at the edge of sleep, and witnesses to the shape of things not yet born. She is the patron of spies, dreamers, outcasts, and those who know that the darkest shadow is also the safest cloak.

names_across_regions.mistlands: The Bell-Shrouded, whose unknotted rope holds the fog at bay
names_across_regions.aeler: The Deep Listener, to whom miners whisper before descending into new shafts
names_across_regions.zakov: The Tide Watcher, a smuggler's patron who hides cargo from the Salt Prince's collectors

lore.quote: Blow out the candle. If the room listens back, ask softly. At the next crossroads, the raven waits – and the shadow remembers your passing.

domain_focus: Latent Potential: the power of what is not yet, the seed of action, the whisper before the scream
Shadow as Shelter: concealment, secrets, and the spaces between notice
Thresholds of Change: doors, crossroads, dreams, and the boundaries of sleep
Raven's Witness: omens, messages, and the weight of secrets shared

thiasos.description: Ikasha's Thiasos is a small creature of shadow and stillness: a black cat with silver eyes that sees in perfect darkness, a gray mouse that nests in the walls of confessionals, a small owl whose feathers drink the light, a pale moth that appears only when a secret is spoken, or a raven chick with one white feather that knows the way to every crossroads.
thiasos.care: Beyond its ordinary care, this Thiasos must spend at least an hour each day in absolute darkness (a closed drawer, a shuttered room). If that need goes unmet, the Thiasos becomes Compromised: it grows restless and fidgets in light, imposing –1 die on all Stealth rolls for its bearer until appeased with a secret whispered in the dark.

codex.description: Ikasha keeps no Codex that resembles a book read by lamplight. It may be a sheaf of blank pages that fill with whispered secrets only when the reader sleeps, a set of black silk ribbons knotted in patterns that change with the moon, or a slate that shows fading images of thresholds crossed.
codex.upkeep: Because Ikasha's truths are written in the unwitnessed, the Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week in a dark room, letting the Codex rest in shadow, or the Rites stored there become faint (treat as Compromised until re-darkened).

patrons_gift.name: Ikasha's Whisper
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of Ikasha may touch a held item (weapon, tool, or garment) and whisper a word of unlight.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Stealth or Deception rolls, and the first time each scene the bearer would be spotted by a mundane observer, they may reroll the opposed check (the shadow bends around them).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to Ikasha.

rites.name: Rite of the Unlit Candle
rites.materials: A candle snuffed with a whisper.
rites.effect: You step into the space between notices. Gain +1 die to a single Stealth or Subterfuge roll, and if you succeed, you may also declare one minor detail 'forgotten' by any observer (e.g., 'they don't remember my face,' 'they left the key in the lock').
rites.push_it: Extend the effect to one ally within Near, but your shadow lingers independently for a moment – the GM gains 1 SB (Diamonds) as evidence remains. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Crossroads Raven
rites.materials: Three black feathers scattered at a crossing.
rites.effect: A raven appears, visible only to you and your allies. It offers an omen: you may reroll one failed navigation, pursuit, or escape roll this scene, or force one enemy to hesitate (lose their next minor action).
rites.push_it: The raven whispers a true secret about the current situation (the GM must answer one yes/no question truthfully). In return, it demands a secret from you – the GM gains 1 SB (Hearts) to spend later as a complication involving that secret. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Umbral Reservoir
rites.materials: Water gathered on a moonless night, held in a black vessel.
rites.effect: Draw on deep reserves of patience and shadow. Choose one: Gain +2 dice on your next Stealth, Deception, or Resolve roll; Clear 1 Fatigue from yourself or a touched ally; Gain one free success on an attempt to escape restraint or pursuit (no roll needed).
rites.push_it: Apply two benefits instead of one, but you mark +1 Obligation and the GM gains 1 SB (Clubs) as the shadow's debt comes due. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Unlatched Secret
rites.materials: A key that has never been used, bent in a circle, or a lock of hair / personal token / name written on black paper.
rites.effect: Choose one: Unlatched Door: Persuade a mundane threshold to open. One lock, seal, or barrier (door, chain, shutter, even a pursuer's grip) opens or loosens as if never secured. Does not work on magical wards. Secret Keeper: Compel a truthful answer to one direct question about a secret the target knows. They resist with Resolve (DV 4). On failure, they answer truthfully (cryptically permitted). On success, they suffer 1 Fatigue from concealment.
rites.push_it: If you chose Unlatched Door, you may also silence any noise the opening makes, but the threshold 'remembers' you – the GM gains 1 SB (Spades) for a later complication. If you chose Secret Keeper, you also learn a hidden emotion or related secret (GM's choice), but the target learns one of your secrets – the GM gains 1 SB (Hearts) to reveal it later. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Umbral Dream
rites.materials: Stand in absolute darkness or at a deserted crossroads at midnight; or burn a vivid dream written down.
rites.effect: You become a living shadow or reach into latent potential. Choose one: Shadow Form: For the scene, you are intangible to mundane harm, can pass through small gaps and thresholds, gain +2 dice to all Stealth rolls, and automatically succeed on one escape attempt. You cannot manipulate objects normally, and you cannot carry items through shadows or bring objects with you when you become intangible. Any items you are carrying fall to the ground (or to the surface you were on) when you assume this form; you may retrieve them after the effect ends. Whisper of Possibility: Once before the next dawn, reroll any single roll after seeing the result (before outcome is declared). The GM gains 1 SB as fate wavers. Hidden Path: You and allies bypass one major obstacle (guarded gate, collapsed bridge, social dead end) as if a secret way had always been there – the GM gains 1 SB as the world adjusts. Unspoken Name: Learn the true name of one creature or place (GM discretion). That name can be used for future rites or bargains.
rites.push_it: Apply two benefits instead of one. If you chose Shadow Form, you may also interact once with a locked or warded object while intangible, but your next defense roll is Desperate. In all cases, the GM gains 2 SB (the dream's echoes attract attention). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of Ikasha sings in whispers – melodies that are felt rather than heard, harmonies that slip beneath the threshold of attention. Their voice is used to hide a crowd's escape, to make a guard forget why they entered a room, or to pass a message through enemy lines without a single word being spoken aloud. Ikasha's Cantors are rarely recognized; they are the ones who hum absently while others plan rebellion.

cult.name: The Cult of the Unlit Candle
cult.description: Ikasha's cults are shadowy by necessity, meeting in basements, abandoned bell-towers, and fog-bound crossroads. They whisper freedom to the oppressed – escaped slaves, hunted heretics, debtors fleeing their creditors. A ritual of the Unlit Candle involves each member extinguishing a flame and speaking a secret wish for escape. The candles are never relit; the wish is carried away on ravens' wings. Their creed is never written, only passed from shadow to shadow: 'The dark does not confine – it conceals the road that the light would forbid.' Outsiders who stumble into a meeting are offered a black feather and a choice: forget, or follow.

witchcraft.name: The Way of Shadow
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with Ikasha is a threshold-keeper or shadow-weaver – one who knows that a door left unlatched is not an invitation to theft, but to liberation. Their magic works in the gaps: the crack under a door, the moment between heartbeats, the pause between a guard's patrol. This craft can be invisible – a bent lock, a misplaced key, a shadow that moves of its own accord – or as grand as erasing a name from a pursuer's memory.
witchcraft.lore: The shadow-weaver's path is the art of the unseen. They learn that the most powerful spell is the one that leaves no trace – a door that opens silently, a guard that forgets, a secret that was never spoken. Ikasha teaches that power is not in the act, but in the space between acts.
witchcraft.quote: The dark does not confine – it conceals the road that the light would forbid.

ravens_quill.name: The Raven's Quill
ravens_quill.description: A quill carved from a raven's primary feather, dipped not in ink but in the absence of light. Once per session, when used to write a name on a threshold (a doorframe, a gatepost, a windowsill), that name becomes 'forgotten' for a scene: the person whose name is written cannot be perceived by those who cross that threshold until they succeed on a Resolve test (DV 3). The quill can also erase a single word from a written document (it becomes a smudge of shadow).

hedge_gifts.name: Unlatched
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, you may declare a mundane lock, latch, or binding to be 'unlatched' – it opens freely (or fails to close) as if it had never been secured. This works on doors, chains, shutters, and even a pursuer's grip, but not on magical wards.

hedge_gifts.name: Shadow Meld
hedge_gifts.description: Once per session, step into any shadow larger than yourself and emerge from another shadow within Near range. You cannot be targeted while moving between shadows.

hedge_gifts.name: Whisper in the Dark
hedge_gifts.description: When in darkness or dim light, you may send a sentence of up to eight words to a willing target within Near range. The target hears it as if whispered beside them. No one else hears it.

monastic_tradition.name: The Way of the Unstruck Bell
monastic_tradition.description: The Unstruck Bell tradition teaches that the greatest defense is to not be where the strike lands. Followers of this path learn to read the gaps in perception, to become forgettable, and to move through shadows as if the shadows themselves had parted for them.

basic.name: Shadow Meld
basic.description: Once per session as an action, step into any shadow larger than yourself and emerge from another shadow within Near range. You cannot be targeted while moving between shadows.

advanced.name: The Unobserved
advanced.description: When you are Hidden, social Story Beats cannot be used to frame you for a crime you did not commit (unless you act first). Additionally, witnesses suffer -2 dice to recall your face or describe you to authorities.

master.name: Threshold of Sleep
master.description: Once per session, walk through a locked door, a guarded threshold, or a magical ward as if it were mist. This does not work on barriers specifically enchanted against shadow-walking (GM discretion).

corruption.benefit: +1 die to Stealth in dim light or darkness.
corruption.cost: Light Sensitivity: -1 die to Stealth in direct sunlight.

corruption.benefit: Once per scene, treat a failed Stealth roll as a success.
corruption.cost: The Witness Debt: A raven appears to watch your next crime. If you fail that roll, the raven reports to a rival.

corruption.benefit: +2 dice to resist being tracked or identified.
corruption.cost: Shadow Lag: Your shadow moves half a second behind you. Those who notice suffer -1 die to social rolls with you.

corruption.benefit: Once per session, become Hidden in plain sight (no roll required) in a crowd.
corruption.cost: Hollow Attention: The Hollow begins to notice your erasures. GM gains 1 SB to spend on a pursuit complication.

corruption.benefit: Immune to mundane forms of surveillance (scrying, tracking dogs, witnesses).
corruption.cost: Forgetful: You occasionally forget minor details of your own past. Mark 1 Fatigue when this happens.

corruption.benefit: Once per session, become intangible to mundane harm for one scene.
corruption.cost: Shadow's Price: Mark +2 Obligation to Ikasha. Your reflection no longer appears in mirrors.

corruption.benefit: Shadow's Whisper: +1 die to Deception when lying in darkness or through intermediaries.
corruption.cost: Truth Echoes: Occasionally speak in riddles or half-truths without realizing it.

corruption.benefit: Umbral Sight: Once per scene, gain +2 dice to Notice hidden threats or ambushes in dim light.
corruption.cost: Light Sensitivity: –1 die to rolls requiring keen vision in bright conditions.

corruption.benefit: Raven's Memory: Never forget a secret told to you; recall any whispered conversation perfectly.
corruption.cost: Secret Burden: Must keep one troubling secret per Tier; suffer 1 Fatigue when actively trying to forget.

corruption.benefit: Threshold Walker: Once per session, move through one locked door, sealed letter, or magical barrier without triggering wards.
corruption.cost: Crossroads Bound: Must pause at literal or metaphorical crossroads to 'listen' before major decisions.

corruption.benefit: Shadow Debt: Once per session, call in a favor from someone who owes you a secret – no questions asked.
corruption.cost: Obligation Web: Every secret you learn creates a subtle tie to its keeper; mark 1 SB (Diamonds) when ignoring these connections.

corruption.benefit: Umbral Ascendancy: Once per session, become completely undetectable to all non-magical senses for one scene.
corruption.cost: Reality Thinning: The boundary between what is and what could be grows thin – the GM may introduce subtle reality alterations around you.

playstyle_notes.description: Ikasha supports infiltration, escape, and patient preparation. Her followers open a door or place a secret, then let others decide whether to use it. Bring her attention through a recurring dream, a raven at an inconvenient window, or a forgotten confidence resurfacing. Her withdrawal feels like an opportunity closing: the guard stays at the door, or the expected shadow is gone.
emphasizes: Latent Potential: power as possibility, not force
Shadow as Shelter: concealment, secrets, and the spaces between notice
Thresholds of Change: doors, crossroads, dreams, and the boundaries of sleep
Raven's Witness: omens, messages, and the weight of secrets shared

sample_adventure.title: The Raven's Bargain
sample_adventure.description: A raven arrives with a black feather tied around a sealed letter. Inside is the name of a person a rival faction intends to erase from the city's records. Protecting them will expose a route used by other fugitives; leaving the records office untouched gives the faction until dawn. The bird waits on the sill while the party decides whom to trust with the name.
sample_adventure.quote: The dark does not confine – it conceals the road that the light would forbid. Choose carefully, for the road you take will remember you.

guises.name: The Deep Listener
guises.note: A dark recess is left beside the place where a shift reports what it encountered. The speaker names the working, not the thing that may be listening. A keeper can preserve a report their superior refused to hear. They cannot demonstrate that everything omitted from the official account has therefore reached a benevolent listener.

guises.name: The Bell-Shrouded
guises.note: A cloth is laid across a bell that should remain silent that night. People attend to the road, the weather, and the person who has not come home. They do not explain the sleep beneath the custom. A sound from under the cloth is not automatically an invitation to remove it.

guises.name: The Tide-Watcher
guises.note: A raven on a dark post marks a place where people wait without lighting the landing. Some seek passage, others news of a vessel. A message can arrive in a familiar voice from an unoccupied boat. The keepers ask what it said before asking whom it sounded like, and seldom settle the second question.

guises.name: The Listener Without a Roll
guises.note: The Unlit Candle reaches people afraid to say a name where an Esoiti may hear it. A whispered plea can be an act of resistance without becoming a reliable escape route. Black Hand agents, the magi, and those hiding from them do not form one interest merely because they all value secrecy. An answer that names a danger does not promise protection from it.

guises.name: The Keeper of the Unspoken Page
guises.note: Some keepers preserve a blank leaf between copied passages and remember why it was left there. Others insist this is a local archive practice mistakenly attributed to Ikasha by foreigners. The disagreement has not prevented a whispered question from being heard in a room whose occupants all believed they were alone.

provenance.origin: Her public cults inherit accounts of the Sleeper rather than a complete history of why she sleeps.
provenance.summary: Some prayers ask that Ikasha remain undisturbed; others that she hear without waking. The difference has produced arguments among people who have received answers neither can explain. Temple compilers have tried to turn these fragments into a continuous divine biography. Her keepers preserve the fragments, including incompatible ones, and generally decline to endorse the finished account.
provenance.the_migration: Night workers, travelers, and households concealing a persecuted guest carried the Unlit Candle's observances across borders. The object is small enough to hide and ordinary enough to explain. Along Zakov's crossings, waiting for a boat gave the Sleeper a maritime title. In Ashaan, people facing the removal of names found a listener who did not demand that a public office first recognize the speaker. That is a reason for the cult's appeal, not an immunity to erasure.
provenance.why_it_took: Keeping a secret can shelter someone or preserve a wrong. The Unlit Candle's houses disagree about when testimony must be brought into daylight. Some have saved people whose names they never recorded; others have enabled a protector to control every account of what happened inside. A listener who never asks whether the speaker may leave has made silence serve a different purpose.
provenance.note: Preserve the boundary around Ikasha's deeper history. These local beliefs do not disclose a hidden cosmological identity, resolve the origin of her sleep, or make every raven, shadow, or absent name her deliberate intervention.

philosophy.name: A Place to Speak Quietly
philosophy.summary: Ikasha offers the possibility of being heard without being displayed. What hears is not necessarily accountable to the person who needed that shelter.
philosophy.the_point: Her devotees can confuse secrecy with safety. A person protected from an official's scrutiny may become dependent on a keeper whose conduct nobody else can examine.
philosophy.the_third_thing: The useful distinction is between controlling access to one's own account and giving someone else the only surviving version. Silence chosen in danger need not become silence owed for life.
philosophy.at_the_table: Introduce an answer that can be checked in part: a location, a name, or a detail of an event. Leave the answering presence uncertain. Let characters decide whom to trust with what they learn rather than forcing revelation or concealment as the only faithful response.
